data.name: Marichi
data.long_meaning: Marichi is the name of the demon son of the Sun God, Surya. He is also known as Maricha and Marichi Makhadev. In Hindu mythology, Marichi is described as a powerful asura, a class of demons. He was a great sage, known for his wisdom and bravery. Marichi is said to have played a significant role in the churning of the ocean of milk, where he was rewarded with the horse, the celestial vehicle of Indra, the god of rain.

data.cultural_impact: Marichi is an essential figure in Hindu mythology, and his name holds significant cultural significance. He is a symbol of courage, strength, and wisdom, representing the power and complexity of the demonic forces that exist within the universe. The tale of Marichi's role in the churning of the ocean of milk is a well-known episode in Hindu mythology, and it illustrates the idea of all beings, divine or demonic, contributing to the creation of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: Marichi embodies the spiritual significance of knowledge, wisdom, and the power of will. He is a reminder that even the most early and seemingly evil beings can be redeemed and rewarded for their contributions. Additionally, Marichi's association with the Sun God represents the importance of the role of knowledge in spiritual growth and enlightenment.
